title: Epochal kernel scout and latency concierge for arch/seq-len autotuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current kernel selection uses a mix of static heuristics and short-lived probes that underperform on sustained, customer-specific traffic patterns (bursts, mixed seq-len). We see tail latency regressions on mixed workloads when kernel choices oscillate during ramp-ups.

Proposal: Implement an 'Epochal Kernel Scout' service plus a 'Latency Concierge' safety layer. The Scout aggregates epochal heatmaps (time-windowed fingerprints) per model + deployment class (arch, chiplet config, quantization profile) and maintains a lightweight, rolling score for kernel candidates across seq-len buckets. The Concierge enforces latency SLOs by hedging (run short decode fallback on alternative kernels with less batching) and triggering a fast rollback if SLO drift is detected.

Objectives:
- Produce per-customer, per-arch kernel recommendations that adapt over epochs (configurable window: 5–60 minutes).
- Smooth kernel switches to avoid oscillation while enabling continuous improvement.
- Provide explainable telemetry (why one kernel chosen) and safe rollouts with automatic rollback.

Why different from existing work: Instead of probing per-request or using monolithic bandits, the Scout summarizes microbench and live telemetry into epochal distributions, enabling robust decisions for infrequent but high-cost seq-len buckets and separating exploration cadence from request-level latency constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Epochal Scout runs and produces kernel scorecards for each model-arch pair at 5-minute cadence
At least 2x improvement in kernel stability (measured as reduced switch-rate) on mixed-burst traces in staging
Latency Concierge prevents >5% SLA breach during controlled kernel rollouts in perf lab
Scout exposes a /recommendations API and a change log; recommendations map to kernel identifiers used by runtime
End-to-end e2e test (simulated bursts) demonstrates rollback within 60s when latency drift exceeds threshold
tasks: Design epochal heatmap schema and storage (sparse histogram per seq-len bucket)
Implement Scout microbench harness to run candidate kernels with representative input (prefill+decode fragments)
Integrate live-telemetry fusion: combine microbench results with sampled production traces using exponentially weighted averaging
Build recommendation API and a small in-memory cache for fast lookup in runtime path
Implement Latency Concierge guardrails: hedging paths, slow-start throttle, and rollback trigger logic
Create rollout plan and gating checks in Console for canary and staged rollout
Add observability: per-recommendation confidence, historical heatmap visualization, and cost/latency tradeoff chart
notes: We should reuse metric namespaces from telemetry-team to avoid duplication (token_latency.p50/p95, kernel_switch.count)
Estimate assumes access to an internal microbench fleet and ~2 FTEs for 6 weeks plus infra support
Edge cases: tiny workloads (seq-len < 8) should prefer low-overhead kernels; very long sequences require separate long-run trials
We must coordinate with Dedicated infra to ensure Scout microbench scheduling doesn't impact customer capacity
metrics: kernel_switch_rate: reduce by 2x on mixed-burst tests
prefill_decode_p95: no worse than baseline+5% during rollout
recommendation_confidence: median > 0.7 for seq-len buckets with >1% traffic
cost_delta: documented expected per-token cost delta for recommended kernel
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Offline analysis: run Scout on historical traces for top 10 models (1 week)
Stage 1 - Perf lab: microbench + simulated bursts against runtime; validate hedging behavior
Stage 2 - Canary: enable recommendations for 5 internal tenants with monitoring and auto-rollback rules
Stage 3 - Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% traffic over two weeks with safety gates
Stage 4 - GA: export recommendations to Console and enable opt-in for Dedicated customers
qa_checklist: Unit tests for heatmap aggregation logic
Integration tests for recommendation API with mocked telemetry
Chaos test: inject slowdown in primary kernel and verify Concierge rolls back
Load test: ensure Scout compute does not add >1% overhead to control plane
Security review of recommendation storage (sensitive customer fingerprints)
